headline: Myanmar junta agrees to take back Rohingya refugees from Bangladesh
summary: The military government in Myanmar has finally agreed to the repatriation of Rohingya people currently residing in Bangladesh.
details: The Myanmar junta government has officially agreed to take back the Rohingya refugees who have sought shelter in Bangladesh.
This development comes after years of diplomatic efforts and pressure to ensure the safe and voluntary return of the displaced population to their homeland.
The repatriation process is expected to address the long-standing humanitarian crisis that has seen millions of Rohingya fleeing violence in Myanmar.
Further details regarding the timeline and the specific mechanisms for the return process are expected to be announced as the process moves forward.
caption:
A major diplomatic breakthrough: Myanmar has finally agreed to take back Rohingya refugees from Bangladesh.

The Myanmar junta government has officially agreed to take back the Rohingya refugees who have sought shelter in Bangladesh.

This development comes after years of diplomatic efforts and pressure to ensure the safe and voluntary return of the displaced population to their homeland.

The repatriation process is expected to address the long-standing humanitarian crisis that has seen millions of Rohingya fleeing violence in Myanmar.

Further details regarding the timeline and the specific mechanisms for the return process are expected to be announced as the process moves forward.

headline_marked: 300,000 Rohingya to be [[repatriated from Bangladesh]] to Myanmar
headline: 300,000 Rohingya to be repatriated from Bangladesh to Myanmar
summary: Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim claims Myanmar has agreed to take back refugees from both Bangladesh and Malaysia.
details: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has announced that Myanmar has agreed to take back 300,000 Rohingya refugees from Bangladesh.
Additionally, Anwar stated that Myanmar has also agreed to repatriate 5,000 Rohingya refugees currently residing in Malaysia.
The Prime Minister emphasized that these developments are the result of careful diplomacy and the maintenance of good relations with Myanmar.
These remarks were made during a meeting with local voters in Chennah on Wednesday.
caption:
300,000 Rohingya refugees are set to return to Myanmar from Bangladesh, according to Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim.

Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has announced that Myanmar has agreed to take back 300,000 Rohingya refugees from Bangladesh.

Additionally, Anwar stated that Myanmar has also agreed to repatriate 5,000 Rohingya refugees currently residing in Malaysia.

The Prime Minister emphasized that these developments are the result of careful diplomacy and the maintenance of good relations with Myanmar.

These remarks were made during a meeting with local voters in Chennah on Wednesday.
